title: TSS ConformanceClaim Schema
description: A versioned, explicit claim of conformance to TSS and related specs. Defined by TSS v1.2.0 §5.11 and §12, extended for multi-axis claims (v1.2) and evidence-bearing levels (v1.3). TSS T-level is the primary audit standard; QSM C-level, THRIVE H-level, QSM-FAI L-level, QSM-ARCH A-level, and Layer Maturity M-level are independent axes (see TSS Appendix Z and specs/QSM-LAYER-MATURITY.md). From v1.3 each claimed level SHOULD be stated as an object carrying the minimum-conformance rules it satisfies and the artifact that satisfies each. A bare string level remains valid for ONE release and is deprecated: the reference evaluator warns on it. Rationale: a level given as a bare string is a number you type; a level carrying rule-by-rule evidence is a number you have to justify, and the second cannot be filled in without discovering the field or object it depends on does not exist.

context_types.description: Context types supported (TSS-CONF-03). Enum matches schemas/context.schema.json. QSM_META is included because QSM §6.1 QSM-META-01 describes 'an implementation supporting QSM_META', so an implementation may legitimately claim it; QSM-FAI PROHIB-06 separately bars an AGENT from acting under one, which is why schemas/fiduciary-context-v1.1.schema.json correctly omits it.

conformance_level.description: Primary TSS audit level (TSS-CONF-04). Minimum-conformance rules: TSS-01..TSS-05 (TSS §12.3).

oneOf.description: DEPRECATED bare form (schema v1.2 and earlier). Accepted for one release per TSS §14.2; the reference evaluator emits a deprecation warning. Migrate to the object form.
Evidence-bearing form. `evidence` cites the minimum-conformance rules this level rests on and, for each, the artifact that satisfies it.

qsm_level.description: QSM object conformance level (TSS Appendix Z). Minimum-conformance rules: QSM-01..QSM-05 (QSM §12).

oneOf.description: DEPRECATED bare form (schema v1.2 and earlier). Accepted for one release per TSS §14.2; the reference evaluator emits a deprecation warning. Migrate to the object form.
Evidence-bearing form. `evidence` cites the minimum-conformance rules this level rests on and, for each, the artifact that satisfies it.

thrive_level.description: THRIVE domain conformance level (TSS Appendix Z). Minimum-conformance rules: THRIVE-01..THRIVE-04 (THRIVE §12.2); THRIVE-05..08 are SHOULDs. THRIVE runs one level beyond the shared C/T/L ladder — THRIVE v1.1.0 defines H4 Integrated, which has no C/T/L counterpart because it extends the THRIVE domain model rather than audit rigour. An H4 implementation is at T3.

oneOf.description: DEPRECATED bare form (schema v1.2 and earlier). Accepted for one release per TSS §14.2; the reference evaluator emits a deprecation warning. Migrate to the object form.
Evidence-bearing form. `evidence` cites the minimum-conformance rules this level rests on and, for each, the artifact that satisfies it.

fai_level.description: QSM-FAI domain conformance level (QSM-FAI §8). QSM-FAI defines its levels in prose rather than as a numbered minimum-conformance list, so cite the rule families that actually bind the claimed level — FC-01..05, TEN-01.., ESC-01..04, PROHIB-01..07.

claimant.description: Entity or person filing the claim

implementation_url.description: URL of the implementation this claim describes

source.description: Provenance of this registry entry. A registry entry is a POINTER with a fetched snapshot, not an independent document: the claim's source of truth is the implementation's own claim file. Registry entries that were copies drifted from their sources within weeks of being written — one published a deviation that had become false while omitting three that had become true. content_hash makes that drift detectable instead of invisible.

source_url.description: Where the authoritative claim file lives. May be non-public: an unreachable source is a limit on WHERE the divergence check can run, not a reason to drop the field. The literal "self:registry" declares that this registry entry IS the source of record — the implementation publishes no machine-readable claim file of its own. That is a legitimate state and requires a `note` saying so, because a DECLARED absence of provenance can be reviewed and a silent one cannot.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the canonical JSON of the source claim at fetch time. For "self:registry" entries there is no external source, so this is the empty hash sentinel "sha256:" + 64 zeros.

rule.description: A named rule ID from the spec governing this axis, e.g. ARCH-05, TSS-03, THRIVE-02, ESC-01. Validated by shape, not by a closed enum: QSM-FAI has no numbered minimum-conformance list, and a closed enum in a published schema goes stale on the next spec release. The reference evaluator carries the per-axis rule sets and warns when a claimed level's evidence does not cover them.

satisfied_by.description: The artifact that satisfies the rule — a repository path with an optional line anchor (path/to/file.ts#L12), a URL, or a spec section reference. This is the field that does the work: it cannot be filled in for a rule the implementation does not actually satisfy without the author noticing.

note.description: Optional qualification — partial satisfaction, a caveat, or why this artifact is the right evidence.

evidence.description: At least one rule/artifact pair. An empty evidence array is not a claim with weak evidence; it is a bare level wearing the object form.
